newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A index ends down on company probe.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A index ends down on company probe.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index closed sharply lower on Wednesday with investor confidence dented by an investigation into a major listed company suspected of accounting irregularities, brokers said.
The A share index slid 9.02 points or 2.25 percent to 391.26 on turnover of 7.91 billion yuan, compared with 10.81 billion yuan on Tuesday.
The B share index inched down 0.08 points or 0.05 percent to end at 154.92 points, with turnover falling to HK$55.25 million from Tuesday's HK$74.45 million.
Authorities are probing Hainan Minyuan Agricultural Development Co for alleged violation of accounting rules in its 1996 annual report, Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange suspended trading in the company's A shares pending the investigation, the newspaper said.
"The report on Minyuan soured market sentiment," said one analyst. "Investors pulled funds out of the market to wait for the outcome of the investigation."
Brokers said B shares lost because institutions were reluctant to buy heavily in the corporate reporting season.
On the B share market, retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise was the worst performer, falling HK$0.15 or 2.73 percent to HK$5.35 on volume of 120,300 shares.
Jiangling Motors bucked the trend with a rise of HK$0.11 or 2.95 percent to HK$3.84 on volume of 385,300 shares, and became the biggest gainer.
On the A share market, chicken and feed processor Shenzhen Kondarl, the biggest loser, slid 0.70 yuan or 5.24 percent to 12.65 on trade of 2.61 million shares.
Brokers said new regulations aimed at tightening control over the market cooled speculation in many of the hot A stocks.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission on Tuesday announced a new rule banning anyone caught in insider trading and price rigging from securities business.
